title: HDPE grade transition A→B against the transition matrix: allowance, overrun, no standard; plan target with or without the standard transition time
spec_ref: LA-08; SME Q9, Q10, E1, E3 (EXPERT_REVIEW §1.4); oee_policy transitionAllowanceInPlan (ISO 22400 / GE PLA: a planned grade change within its standard is planned time)

inputs.standardAB: reference 2.1 h (7560 s) = median of illustrative A→B observations 1.8, 2.0, 2.1, 2.3, 2.8 h (SME E1)

notes: The transition loses the capacity of its running time (3 h x 30 t/h = 90 t): the off-grade it made (40 t, its own quality class) and the rate deficit (50 t). The standard allows 2.1 / 3 = 0.7 of each: 0.9 h of overrun = 27 t, the E1 worked example priced at the rate. With a reference off-grade quantity (30 t) the off-grade allowance is bounded in tonnes. Without a matrix entry nothing is invented: all 90 t are excess. With transitionAllowanceInPlan = planned (the oee_policy default from 14 Oct 2026) the campaign plan already deducts the standard transition time: target 177 t = 240 − 2.1 h × 30 t/h, and the planned rate is target ÷ (eligible time − standard transition time) = 30 t/h. The plan ledger then has no allowance line: the 27 t overrun alone closes the 27 t gap, and the 63 t allowance is reported on the plan totals as planned transition time (information, flag transition_allowance_planned). The capacity ledger is the same under both options. A change that finishes inside its standard (02:00-03:30, 20 t off-grade, gross 215, good 195) is all allowance (45 t, no plan line) and gives back the 0.6 h the plan set aside: 18 t above the 177 t target. A policy version written before the option says loss: the allowance stays a plan loss line against the 240 t target, as above. All values are illustrative, not plant data.
